title: Joining Billy Fowler's band at the Club Alabam
summary: He auditions for Billy Fowler's band at the lavish Broadway Club Alabam, among experienced players such as Edgar Sampson, Freddy Johnson, Ward Pinkett and Ed Cuffee.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: So from that point on, and while I'm working up there a few weeks, a fellow offered me a job with Billy Fowler's band at the Club Alabam on Broadway. This was a big-time nightclub down on 44th Street, big show, chorus, showgirls, comedians, a great big band was down there -- Jimmy Wade's band was working in there at the present, and Billy was going to take his place. So I reported for rehearsal down there. And boy, I've never seen nothing so beautiful in all my life. The club was beautiful. All the chorus girls was beautiful! All the show girls was beautiful. Everything was beautiful.

And here's the band now; here's Billy Fowler. I don't know any of them, you know. I don't know Billy. Billy was a helluva nice guy. He had heard about me, and he was glad that I could join the band. Edgar Sampson was in the band. Steeplehead Johnson. He was the piano player.... Freddy Johnson. He had just come back from Europe; he was the piano player. No, he hadn't went to Europe. He was the piano player. A fellow named Ward Pinkett, the trumpet player. Cuffee...
...trombone. Boy, I'm doing pretty good with this band.
Let me see who else was in that band. John Mitchell, guitar. Who was it I didn't name? Did I name the piano player?

The drummer...hmm, I must have knew who he was. And he had to be good to be down there. Because all these cats was what you called sharks, you know. All well-experienced men -- except me. I wonder how I even got in there. And Billy Fowler was a hell of a musician himself. He was a hell of a saxophone player.
Then you must have had a tenor.
I mean, he was in front of the band, you know. Well, there was a tenor...
